source_text: Et post reconciliationem, quam cum Deo habere promeruimus per opera videlicet Mediatoris, debemus percipere animo sempiterna gaudia et non solum salutem sperare, sed etiam gloriam.
pass_a_gloss: And after the reconciliation which we have merited to have with God through the works namely of the Mediator, we ought to perceive with the mind everlasting joys and not only to hope for salvation, but also glory.

lemmas.lexica: LS anima; Blaise human soul as image

pass_b_english: After the reconciliation with God that we have obtained through the Mediator’s works, we should therefore grasp everlasting joys in our minds and hope not only for salvation but also for glory.

choices.why: Image of God in the soul; keep soul not 'mind' or 'life-force'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
